findings.issue: Repeatedly tried to crop the reference PNG via img.screenshot with clip, which Chrome's image document ignores; four or five attempts produced the same squeezed thumbnail before switching to a canvas data-URL export.
findings.suggestion: On the second identically-wrong crop output, switch method (canvas crop → data-URL → file) instead of re-clipping.

findings.issue: Two failed edits against an oldText that never existed — the file was already correct and the agent had misremembered its own write.
findings.suggestion: Grep/read the target lines before editing code just written from memory.

findings.issue: `pkill -f 'node server.mjs'` / `'server.mjs'` matched the bash session's own command line, killing the shell twice (exit 143) and making the cleanup turn take four attempts.
findings.suggestion: Record the PID when backgrounding servers, or use a distinctive pattern that can't match the pkill command itself.

findings.issue: Three turns spent trying to get Pillow installed in an environment with no pip, before discovering it was unnecessary.
findings.suggestion: Check tool availability (`which pip`, `python3 -m pip --version`) before chaining install attempts; fall back to the already-present Playwright sooner.

summary: A disciplined 27-minute session that read the spec, tests, design and data shapes up front, wrote the whole app in one pass, and passed all 54 acceptance tests on the first run with zero fix cycles. It then went well beyond the tests, comparing its own screenshots to all nine reference images pixel-by-pixel and restructuring the Pokémon hero to match. The only real waste was a stretch of fumbling crop tooling on reference PNGs, two edits against text that didn't exist, and a self-killing pkill during cleanup.
